builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: LoopAhead: Speculating Ahead for Faster Decoding in Looped Language Models
summary: It replaces standard autoregressive decoding and pipelined self-speculative decoding in Looped Transformers with a lightweight lookahead drafter that predicts multiple future tokens from early-loop states while deeper loops prune draft branches. The cost is an additional trained drafter module, deeper-loop feedback logic, and verification compute still spent on incorrect speculative branches. It can fail to deliver gains on non-looped architectures, and the speedup depends on drafter acceptance rates, which degrade when early-loop features poorly predict deeper-loop outputs.
rationale: The method is restricted to Looped Transformer architectures, which the reader does not train and which are rarely available as off-the-shelf production models, so adoption is blocked by an architectural prerequisite rather than by implementation effort.
technique: Speculative decoding with early-loop lookahead drafter

claims.statement: It replaces standard autoregressive decoding and pipelined self-speculative decoding in Looped Transformers with a lightweight lookahead drafter that predicts multiple future tokens from early-loop states while deeper loops prune draft branches. The cost is an additional trained drafter module, deeper-loop feedback logic, and verification compute still spent on incorrect speculative branches. It can fail to deliver gains on non-looped architectures, and the speedup depends on drafter acceptance rates, which degrade when early-loop features poorly predict deeper-loop outputs.
LoopAhead achieves up to 7.82x decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding while preserving the target model's output distribution.
